<skill_content name="but">
# Skill: but

# GitButler CLI Skill

Use GitButler CLI (`but`) as the default version-control interface.

## Start Here

Choose the narrowest first command by task; avoid ritual status checks:

```bash
# Selected dirty files/hunks:
but diff

# Commit order, branch/stack placement, conflict overview:
but status

# File IDs, per-commit files, amend details:
but status -fv

# What one applied branch or commit changed, for review:
but diff <branch-or-commit>

# Details for one known branch or commit:
but show <id>
```

Do not run plain `but status` and then `but status -fv` unless the compact output lacks file details needed for the task.

For "commit just/only/specific changes on a new branch", use the fast path:

```bash
but diff
but commit -b <branch> -m "<msg>" <id> <id>
```

`but commit -b <branch> ...` creates the branch when it does not exist and prints the created commit. Do not run a separate `but branch new`, status command, or verification diff unless the task needs workspace information that the result does not provide.

In a linked worktree, such as `.claude/worktrees/*`, omit `-b` so the commit goes on the branch the worktree has checked out. Use that branch as the new branch; do not stack another one on it. A worktree with a detached HEAD has no branch yet. There, `but commit -b <new-name> -m "<msg>"` creates the branch at HEAD, checks it out in that worktree, and commits to it.

## IDs

The first token on each `but diff` / `but status` line is that line's ID. When a command needs an ID, copy it exactly from the current output; never hardcode or invent one. ID lifetimes differ by entity:

- Changes and sources are **positional, space-separated** IDs (`but commit -b feat -m "msg" uvw:2e4 uvw:e2c`). An uncommitted hunk ID is written `<file-id>:<hunk-id>` (e.g. `uvw:2e4`, copied from bare `but diff`) — the part after the colon is the hunk's ID, **not** a line range (`uvw:16-40` is invalid). Do not invent flags like `--changes` / `--hunk` / `--ids`, pass a line range, or comma-separate IDs — `uvw,qyo` is parsed as one ID and fails.
- `but diff` is the exception: it accepts at most **one** target. Bare `but diff` shows all uncommitted files; inspect committed files or other entities one target at a time — never `but diff <id> <id>`.
- A committed file is `<commit-id>:<file-id>` (e.g. `mzm:uvw`, shown under each commit). A committed hunk is `<commit-id>:<file-id>:<hunk-id>` and is shown by `but diff <commit-id>`. `@` means the uncommitted area.
- Commit IDs are stable change IDs that survive history edits (`amend`, `squash`, `move`, `uncommit`, `reword`). Commits without a change ID (e.g. upstream-only) lead with a sha prefix instead, and `#N`-suffixed refs disambiguate duplicates — both go stale after history edits, and a stale sha can silently resolve to the wrong commit. The `(sha …)` on verbose commit lines is informational — do not pass it to commands.
- Branch short IDs are snapshot-local selectors. Use full branch names for branch-targeting mutations; short IDs are safe only for immediate read-only inspection.
- File/hunk IDs copied from one diff read generally remain usable across chained commits. If one stops resolving, re-read `but diff` and retry.

**Chaining:** mutation output is concise by default, so you may chain mutations with `&&` off one inspection read. Do not chain branch short IDs through mutations; use full branch names. Add `--status-after` only when the next step needs workspace IDs or details that the mutation result does not provide. Chained `but commit` calls stack in the order written — the first is oldest, each later one goes on top. History edits may run in sequence when every commit ref involved is a change-ID ref; run them one at a time with `--status-after` when a ref is sha-based or `#N`-suffixed, or when the next command needs freshly issued IDs. Chaining `but uncommit <id> && but diff` is safe because bare `diff` needs no ID from the uncommit output. Never pipe a mutation through `tail` or `head`: the pipeline then exits with their status, so the next `&&` runs even when the mutation failed.

## Non-Negotiable Rules

1. Use `but` for all write operations. Never run `git add`, `git commit`, `git push`, `git fetch`, `git pull`, `git checkout`, `git merge`, `git rebase`, `git stash`, or `git cherry-pick`; `but pull --check` fetches. The only exceptions are selecting a side of a conflicted submodule in resolution mode (see Resolve conflicted commits) and creating a missing target branch (see Notes). If the user says a `git` write command, translate it to `but` and run that.
2. Mutation commands print their result without appending workspace status. Add `--status-after` only when the next step needs resulting workspace IDs or details; otherwise trust the mutation result and do not run a verification status/diff.
3. Branches marked `(merged upstream)` have landed; start new work on another branch. That marker alone does not mean `but pull` removes them: run `but pull --check` first. `but pull` removes only branches listed `[integrated]` ("has been integrated upstream and removed locally", or "has been merged into <target> and removed" when the target has no upstream) and rebases the rest, which stay applied. To clear a landed branch that stays applied, use `but unapply <branch>` (acts on its whole stack) rather than `but discard`. `push` and mutations (`commit`, `amend`, `squash`, `uncommit`, `reword`, `move`) refuse landed branches and commits, `absorb` skips them with a notice, and `commit` skips them when picking a default target.
4. Keep going between routine `but` commands. Put any status note in the same message as the next command, and don't end a turn on a summary that announces the next `but` step without running it. Finish with a concise summary.
5. Prefer this skill and `but skill reference` over exploratory help calls. Use `<command> --help` when required syntax is missing or a command fails; use top-level help only when you genuinely need to discover an undocumented command.
6. Other agents may share this checkout, so `@` can hold their edits. Commit, amend, and discard only the IDs or paths you changed. Bare `but commit`, `but absorb`, `but discard @`, and `git stash` take their work too, and a refusal naming files you didn't edit means you selected theirs.

## Command Patterns

- Initialize a Git repository: `but init` (current directory) or `but -C <path> init`. Non-interactive; creates no commits, remotes, or GitButler workspace. Existing repositories are left unchanged. In a repository with no commits, make the first commit with a bare `but commit -m "<msg>"`; `-b` is refused there.

- Commit: `but commit -b <branch> -m "<msg>" <id> <id>` — `-b <branch>` creates the branch if it does not exist
- Commit everything uncommitted: `but commit -b <branch> -m "<msg>"` (omit the IDs)
- Several commits from one diff: chain `but commit` calls with `&&` (commits stack oldest-first)
- Never pass `-s` to `commit`, `move`, or `pick`: it is `--switch`, not git's `--signoff`, and it unapplies every other stack.
- The branch is never positional (`but commit <branch>` fails; use `-b`), `but amend` always needs `-t`, and `but diff` takes one target (use a shared `dir/` or one call each).
- Commit at a specific history position: `--above <commit-or-branch>` or `--below <commit-or-branch>` (mutually exclusive). With a branch target, add `-b <new-name>` to name the new branch; otherwise its name is generated. The name must not already exist. Do not combine `-b` (even without a name) with commit/worktree targets.
- Targeting is **required** when more than one **stack** is applied; without it `but commit` fails with "Unclear where to commit. Found more than one stack". Several branches stacked together count as one stack — an untargeted commit then silently lands on the stack's top branch, so pass `-b` whenever the branch matters.
- Always pass `-m "<msg>"` (or `-F -` with a heredoc, `-F <file>` with a file outside the repository, or `--no-message`) to `but commit`, and to `but squash` whenever its sources are commits or branches unless the target is `@` (squash also takes `-u` to keep the target's message) — those compose a new message; without a flag an agent run keeps whatever the command composed (empty for `but commit`, the joined source messages for `but squash`) and a terminal opens an editor. Squash sources that are uncommitted or committed changes reuse the target's message and need no flag; squashing into `@` rejects message flags outright.
- Amend: `but amend -t <commit-or-branch> <file-or-hunk-id> <file-or-hunk-id>` — a branch target resolves to its newest commit
- Uncommit: `but uncommit <commit-id>` (whole commit), `but uncommit <branch>` (all commits and remove branch), `but uncommit <commit-id>:<file-id>` (committed file), or `but uncommit <commit-id>:<file-id>:<hunk-id>` (committed hunk); committed files and hunks may be mixed, but all must come from one commit
- Copy commits (sources stay unchanged): `but pick <sha> [<sha>...] -b <new-branch>` puts the copies on a new independent branch from the target, `-b <existing-branch>` on that applied branch's tip, and `--above <branch> -b <new-name>` (or `--below`) on a new branch stacked there. Pick applies sources in the order given, so pass them oldest first. For a branch that is not applied, list SHAs with `git log --reverse <target>..<branch>` and inspect them with `git show` or `but show <sha>`; `but diff` and the IDs that `but branch show` prints for it do not work.
- Move committed changes into an existing commit or `@`: `but squash <commit-id>:<file-id> -t <commit-id-or-@>` for a committed file; `but squash <commit-id>:<file-id>:<hunk-id> -t <commit-id-or-@>` for a committed hunk; all sources must come from one commit
- Move committed changes into a new commit at a chosen position: `but move <commit-id>:<file-id> --above <commit-or-branch> -m "<msg>"` for a committed file; `but move <commit-id>:<file-id>:<hunk-id> --above <commit-or-branch> -m "<msg>"` for a committed hunk (`--below`, `--branch`, and `--unstack` also work)
- `but split` and a `but move` of committed changes name their new commit with `-m` or `-F` too; without either the commit gets an empty message. `but move` rejects `-m`/`-F` for whole-commit and branch sources.
- Move commit to branch top: `but move <commit-id> -b <branch>`
- Move commits or committed changes onto a new named branch: `but move <source> --above <branch> -b <new-name>` (`--below` also works); use `but move <source> --unstack -b <new-name>` for an independent branch. Omit `-b` for a generated name. Naming is not supported when stacking or unstacking a branch source.
- Discard: `but discard <id> [<id>...]` — accepts branches, commits, committed changes, uncommitted changes, or `@` for all uncommitted changes
- Push: `but push <top-branch>` — pushes the selected branch and its ancestors; to update a stack, select its top branch once and never loop. Bare `but push` pushes all unpushed work when run non-interactively — one push per stack (its topmost unpushed branch, ancestors included), and the output lists every branch it pushed. It exits non-zero if any stack failed; stacks that already pushed stay pushed, and rerunning after fixing the failure is safe (up-to-date stacks are skipped). `but push` and `but pr new` replace the remote branch: if others may have pushed to it, bring their commits in first (see Bring in commits pushed to a branch's own remote).
- Create PR: `but pr new <branch-name> [-m "Title..."] [-F - | -F <file>] [-t] [--draft]` — auto-pushes first; do not run `but push` before it

## Task Recipes

### Update workspace from main

For "get latest from main", "update/sync this workspace", "rebase onto main", or "pull main":

1. `but pull` — one command; no preflight needed. Its output reports the resulting state, and `but undo` reverts it. Uncommitted changes that conflict with the update get conflict markers and show as `{conflicted}`; resolve them as in Conflicts in uncommitted files.
2. If commits come back conflicted, resolve them with the `but resolve conflicts <branch>` and `but resolve apply` loop in Resolve conflicted commits, one branch at a time. When `HEAD` is `gitbutler/workspace`, `but pull` prints `but resolve <commit>` as the next step; that is edit mode, which is only for running code against a resolution.

`but pull --check` answers "would this conflict?" without updating. Do not use it as a routine
preflight; use it when the user asks for a preview, you need a fetch, repository policy requires one, other agents'
branches may move, or an applied branch was just merged upstream (see rule 3).

Rebasing applied branches onto the latest target IS `but pull` — never `move`, `config target`, `unapply`, or raw `git pull`/`git rebase`. The base shown in status is the last FETCHED state: when `git log` shows the remote target (for example `origin/main`) ahead of it, that is exactly the update `but pull` fetches and applies — the target setting is not stale and repointing it is never the fix. Pull carries uncommitted changes along; there is no stash, so do not hand-revert files.

### Bring in commits pushed to a branch's own remote

`but pull` only rebases onto the target. Commits someone pushed to your branch's remote show in `but status` under `(upstream: on <remote>/<branch>)`, above the branch's own commits; if status may be stale, run `but pull --check` to fetch.

1. `but branch update <branch>`, once, on the branch they pushed to.
2. Then `but pull` if the target moved too. Update before pulling. If the branch was rebased since its last push (for example by an earlier `but pull`), the update leaves an empty `(no changes)` copy of a shared commit. On a single branch, `but discard` that copy by its `#N` ref. In a stack, `but undo` the update and tell the user, because the update can also move commits into the lower branch. Do not update a second time, even if `(upstream: …)` still lists commits, because a second update duplicates commits.

### Commit selected files or hunks

1. `but diff` — shows file and hunk IDs for uncommitted changes. Do not run plain `but status` first.
2. Use file IDs when whole files belong in the commit; use hunk IDs (`<file-id>:<hunk-id>`) when only part of a file belongs. Omit IDs you don't want committed. For whole files, repo-root paths or a `dir/` prefix work too (`but commit -b feat -m "msg" src/ui/ README.md`; no `./` or globs), so don't build ID lists by piping `but diff` through grep.
3. `but commit -b <branch> -m "<msg>" <id1> <id2>` — the branch is created if it does not exist, so no prior `but branch new` is needed.
4. When the task requires knowing which changes remain, add `--status-after`; otherwise the created-commit result is sufficient.

Edge case: if wanted and unwanted edits are in the same diff hunk, GitButler cannot split that hunk by ID. Only when the task requires keeping part of that hunk uncommitted, temporarily edit the working tree to isolate the wanted lines, commit those IDs, then restore the leftover lines so they remain uncommitted.

### Amend into existing commit

1. `but status -fv` for the target commit ID and file IDs; `but diff` for hunk IDs when only part of a file belongs.
2. `but amend -t <commit-id> <id> <id>` — one command per target commit. For several target commits, chain the amends with `&&` when every target is a change-ID ref; otherwise run them one at a time with `--status-after` to get fresh refs.

### Split an existing commit

For a two-way split, move selected committed files or hunks directly into a new commit:

1. `but diff <source-commit-id>` — read committed file and hunk IDs.
2. `but split <committed-file-or-hunk-id> [<committed-file-or-hunk-id>...] -m "<message>"` — sources may mix files and hunks, but must come from one commit. The command creates the named commit immediately above the source and leaves unselected changes and the original message in the source. No follow-up reword is needed for the new commit.
3. Add `--status-after` only when the next step needs workspace IDs or details not provided by the mutation result.

For more than two replacement commits, repeat `but split ... -m "<message>"` using the remaining source's committed changes, or use the uncommit/recommit workflow below when rebuilding the entire commit:

1. `but status -fv` when you need the source commit, branch name, or placement anchor.
2. `but uncommit <source-commit-id> && but diff` in one shell call exposes the commit's changes and prints the resulting file and hunk IDs.
3. Pick replacement contents from that dirty diff, not from the old committed diff.
4. Determine the requested chronological order from the user's wording, then create the replacement commits oldest-first by chaining `but commit` calls. Do not reverse that order to match `but status`, which displays commits newest-first. `-b <branch>` puts each new commit at the TOP of that branch — if the split commit had commits above it, the replacements now sit above those preserved commits.
5. **If commits from that branch must stay ABOVE the replacements, put the preserved block back on top instead of fighting anchors.** Do not anchor with `--above <top>`/`--below <top>` (sha/`#N` anchors go stale as each insert rewrites history). Move the block together so its internal order stays intact: append `&& but move <preserved-id> [<preserved-id>...] -b <branch>` to the commit chain. Change-ID refs from step 1 stay valid; wait for fresh output first if any preserved ref is sha-based or `#N`-suffixed.
6. Leave unwanted changes uncommitted. Replacements created oldest-first appear newest-first in status — that is correct; do not reorder them. Add `--status-after` to the final mutation when you need to inspect the resulting order.

### Reorder commits

`but status` displays commits newest/top first, while task specs often list history oldest to newest — translate before moving.

1. `but status` once to get commit IDs (use `-fv` only if you also need file details).
2. `but move <source> --below <target-commit>` places source immediately below target in `but status` (older in oldest-to-newest history). `--above` places it immediately above (newer). `but move <source> -b <branch>` moves it to branch top/newest.
3. For an adjacent block, run ONE move, anchored either way: `but move <block-id> <block-id> --below <following-commit-id>` or `but move <block-id> <block-id> --above <preceding-commit-id>`. Pick an anchor outside the block; source order does not matter and the block keeps its internal order. Add `--status-after` when you need to inspect the resulting order; do not move the anchor or block members again.
4. For other reorders, make the smallest set of moves.

### Squash commits

1. `but status` for commit IDs and order.
2. Name the sources positionally and the result/target commit with `-t`: `but squash <source> [<source>...] -t <target> -m "<new message>"`.
3. To collapse an entire branch into one commit, pass just the branch and no `-t`: `but squash <branch> -m "<new message>"`.
4. Multiple independent groups may run in sequence off one status read (targets keep their change-ID refs); prefer newer/top groups first. Take fresh refs only when a ref is sha-based or `#N`-suffixed.
5. Add `--status-after` to the final squash when you need to inspect the resulting history; do not re-verify with a separate status.

### Stack existing branches

To make one existing branch depend on another: `but move <child-branch-name> --above <parent-branch-name>` (use full branch names; commit reordering uses commit IDs). To unstack: `but move <branch-name> --unstack`.

**DO NOT** stack via `uncommit` + `branch delete` + `branch new --above`, and do not use `but undo` to unstack.

### Work in a linked worktree

1. `but worktree new <branch-name>` checks out that branch in a new directory, creating it if needed (an existing branch must not be in the workspace), and prints that directory. Add `-A <branch-or-commit>` to start the branch there instead of the workspace base; it takes any Git revision, like a SHA or `origin/main`. Worktrees made by other tools must sit outside the repository directory or be listed in `.git/info/exclude`; otherwise a bare `but commit` in the main checkout records them in the branch.
2. Run `but` from that directory, or with `but -C <path>`. There, a bare `but commit -m "<msg>"` or `but diff` takes that worktree's changes, a bare path names a file there, and the commit goes on the worktree's branch. Do the work on that branch, also in a worktree another tool made. `-b <new-name>` is refused there, except in a worktree with a detached HEAD, where it names the worktree's branch; stack a new branch on it only when the user asks for a separate branch. `but undo` doesn't restore a branch a worktree has checked out. It refuses, or it reports success and leaves that branch as it is, so undoing a `move` out of the branch leaves the commit on neither branch. Reverse a command that changed the worktree's branch with its inverse (`uncommit`, `reword`, or `move` the commit back), also when you ran it from another checkout.
3. `but status` from any checkout shows the worktree as a lane of its own, with the same IDs everywhere. `@` always means the main worktree's uncommitted changes; `<worktree>:@` names a linked worktree's changes from anywhere.
4. Push and open PRs as for any branch (`but pr new <branch-name>`). `but pull` also rebases worktree branches. If that leaves a worktree commit `{conflicted}`, the branch name doesn't find it: take its commit ID from `but status` and run `but resolve conflicts <commit-id>`, then `but resolve apply <path>:<N> --commit <commit-id>`.
5. When done, `but worktree remove <name>` deletes the directory and keeps the branch. It refuses while the worktree has uncommitted changes; `-f` discards them. To delete the branch as well, run `but branch delete <name>` afterwards.

### Create or manage pull requests

`but pr new <branch-name>` pushes the selected branch and its ancestors, then creates the PR in one step — no prior `but push`. Provide `-F -` with a heredoc or `-F <file>` (first line is the title), `-t`, or `-m` with real newlines (zsh/bash: `-m $'Title\n\nBody'`) so no editor opens. Do not write the message to a file inside the repository: the next `but commit` would commit it. If forge auth is missing, ask the user to run `but config forge auth` in a terminal; it refuses non-interactive runs.

If you do create a PR for a stacked branch, use `but pr` — not `gh pr create` (only `but pr` sets PR bases and stack metadata; `gh pr create` breaks that). To publish a whole stack: `but pr new <top-branch-name> -t`. Manage with `but pr auto-merge|set-draft|set-ready <selector>`; selectors can be a branch name, current branch/stack CLI ID, or numeric review ID. See `but skill reference` for details.

When `but pr new` prints a `<pr-created>` line, copy that line into the text of your reply. It tells the app running you that this session opened the PR.

If you run in the Claude desktop app, end the `but pr new` line with the shell comment `# gh pr create`, for example `but pr new <branch-name> -F - <<'EOF' # gh pr create`. While `gitbutler/workspace` is checked out, the app counts a PR as opened by this session only when the command text contains `gh pr create`.

### Dependency conflict with another branch

Changes that build on another branch's commits cannot land on an independent branch. `but commit` and `but amend` fail atomically ("Cannot commit: N changes could not be applied"), naming the branch and commit each rejected change depends on — nothing is committed and no `-b` branch is created.

Stack only when your change builds on that branch's code. A refusal can also mean your hunk only borders lines that branch changed (a doc line, a lockfile): then leave one unchanged line between your edit and theirs, or keep that hunk uncommitted until that branch lands, and commit the rest. Never drop or rewrite real work to get past a refusal; ask the user.

When there is a single dependency branch, the error's Hint gives the exact recovery command: `but move <your-branch> --above <dependency-branch>` to stack an existing branch on its dependency, or `but branch new <name> --above <dependency-branch>` when the target branch didn't exist yet. Run it, then retry the original command. When the error names dependencies without a Hint (several dependency branches, or the dependency is on the target branch itself), run `but status -fv` to see where the dependent commits live before choosing a placement.

If that recovery command fails, do NOT try `uncommit`, `squash`, or `undo` as a workaround — re-run `but status -fv` to confirm both branches exist and are applied, then retry with exact branch names.

### Resolve conflicted commits (after pull, move, or reorder)

**NEVER use `git add`, `git commit`, `git checkout --theirs/--ours`, or any git write command during resolution.** Only `but resolve` commands plus direct file edits. The one exception is a conflicted submodule in edit mode, below.

Conflicts do not interrupt operations in GitButler: a rebase always completes, and commits that conflicted are marked `{conflicted}` in `but status`. Find them from the warning that history-editing commands (`move`, `discard`, …) print, from the `but pull` summary, or from `but status`. Resolve them one conflict at a time, without entering any mode. Resolve any uncommitted `{conflicted}` files first, as in Conflicts in uncommitted files; `apply` refuses while one is left. Work through one branch at a time, oldest commit first — the loop is:

1. `but resolve conflicts <branch>` — shows the conflicts of that branch's oldest conflicted commit, numbered per file. Each conflict has three sections: `ours` (the new base the commit was rebased onto), `base` (common ancestor), and `theirs` (the commit's own version). Without a branch it picks the first conflicted branch and tells you which; the output also says when other conflicted commits exist.
2. Apply one resolution per command:
   - Merged/mixed content (the common case — combine the intent of both sides): pipe it to `but resolve apply <path>:<N>` via stdin (heredoc) or pass `--file <f>`. The content replaces the whole conflicted region; never include conflict markers.
   - Take a side entirely: `but resolve apply <path>:<N> --ours` or `--theirs` (bare `<path>` applies the side to all conflicts in that file).
   - Delegate one conflict to the configured AI model: `but resolve apply <path>:<N> --ai` — prefer your own merged content when you have the context.
   - `apply` targets the same default commit as `conflicts`; when more than one branch is conflicted, pin it with `--commit <branch>`.
3. Go back to step 1 until it reports no conflicts. Commit ids are not stable here — every apply rewrites the commit — but branch names are, so address everything by branch and never bookkeep commit ids. Partial progress is fine: a commit with unresolved conflicts left stays `{conflicted}` with exactly those conflicts.

A wrong resolution is reverted with `but undo`.

`but resolve <commit-id> --ai` resolves a whole commit with the configured AI model in one shot, and `but resolve --ai` without a commit resolves every conflicted commit, oldest first — acceptable as a fallback, but you usually have better context than that model does, so prefer resolving the conflicts yourself with `apply`.

**Use edit mode only when you must run code against the resolution** (build/tests at that commit). Edit mode needs `gitbutler/workspace`: while a single branch is checked out, `but resolve <commit-id>` refuses, so use `apply`.

1. `but resolve <commit-id>` — enters resolution mode and prints the conflict regions.
2. **Edit the files** to remove every conflict marker — `<<<<<<<`, `|||||||` (the common-ancestor section), `=======` and `>>>>>>>` — and keep the correct content. Do NOT skip this; do NOT use `but amend` on conflicted commits.
   - A conflicted submodule has no markers and `finish` refuses until you select its side: see Conflict Resolution Mode in `but skill concepts`.
3. `but resolve finish` reports leftover markers, surviving uncommitted changes, every remaining conflicted commit, and the exact current `but resolve <id>` command. Add `--status-after` to the finish you expect to clear the last conflict only when the task needs the complete resulting workspace. When it says no conflicted commits remain, stop; do not run a verification status. Cancel instead with `but resolve cancel --force`, which drops your resolution edits; without `--force` it refuses once the conflict markers are checked out.
4. Repeat for remaining conflicted commits, oldest first — finishing a lower commit rebases the ones above it.

### Conflicts in uncommitted files

`but status` marks uncommitted files with unresolved merge conflicts `{conflicted}`; they are excluded from committable changes and outside `but resolve` mode. Edit the file to the wanted contents with no conflict markers left (or delete it), then `but resolve <path>...` to mark it resolved with that state; it then shows as an ordinary uncommitted change.

## Git-to-But Map

| git | but |
|---|---|
| `git status` | `but status` for branch/stack/commit overview; `but status -fv` for file details; `but diff` for selected dirty changes |
| `git add` + `git commit` | `but commit -b <branch> -m ... <ids>` |
| `git checkout -b` + commit | `but commit -b <new-branch> -m ... <ids>` |
| `git push` | `but push <branch-name>` |
| `git rebase -i` | `but move`, `but squash`, `but reword` |
| `git rebase --onto` | `but move <branch> --above <new-base>` |
| `git checkout -- <file>` / `git restore` | `but discard <path>`, or a hunk ID from `but diff` |
| `git cherry-pick` | `but pick` |
| `git fetch` | `but pull --check` (fetches; changes no branch) |
| `git pull` on a branch others pushed to | `but branch update <branch>`, then `but pull` |
| `git worktree add -b <branch>` | `but worktree new <branch>` |
| `git worktree remove` | `but worktree remove <name>` |
| `gh pr create` | `but pr new <branch-name> -m "Title..."` |

## Notes

- `but` needs no setup in a Git repository. `HEAD` is either one checked-out branch, marked `[HEAD]` in `but status`, or `gitbutler/workspace`, which merges every applied stack. Applying a second stack, or applying a branch while the target branch is checked out, switches to `gitbutler/workspace`; unapplying back to one stack checks that branch out again. Commands and IDs are the same either way. It does need a local branch tracking the remote's default branch: if commands fail with "No target branch is configured", run `but config target origin/main` (with the default branch's name), which creates `main` to track it if missing. Never `git branch --set-upstream-to` on your own branch, which makes that branch the target.
- `but undo` restores the whole snapshot, so uncommitted edits made after the undone operation are lost (`but redo` brings them back). Commit them first.
- Read-only git inspection (`git log`, `git blame`, `git show --stat`) is allowed.
- If `but` prints an `AGENT ACTION REQUIRED` skill warning, run the suggested command once, then reload/use the GitButler skill. If it repeats, report it instead of retrying.
- For command syntax and flags: `but skill reference`
- For workspace model: `but skill concepts`

1: defmodule Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.Commands.Schedule do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   The workshop lifecycle commands of the Beginners' Workshop boundary
4:   (ALE-405): `schedule_workshop`, `update_workshop`, `reschedule_workshop`,
5:   `cancel_workshop`, `pause_batches` and `resume_batches`, all
6:   `beginners.workshops.manage`. `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.Commands` authorizes
7:   the actor and routes here; every body runs inside `Commands.Protocol`.
8: 
9:   ## Schedule and update
10: 
11:   `schedule_workshop` creates up to 20 workshops in one transaction (a
12:   failure names the 0-based workshop: `{:workshop, index, reason}`), each
13:   with optional Staff. `update_workshop` edits capacity, fee, Payment
14:   Cutoff, contact-from date and window length before Attendance
15:   Finalisation: lowering capacity below the seats taken is
16:   `:capacity_below_taken`, a fee once people were contacted `:fee_locked`,
17:   a contact-from date once Batch 1 went out `:contact_from_locked`, and an
18:   earlier cutoff ends an open Batch window with it. The attributes are the
19:   `Commands.command/0` typedoc's.
20: 
21:   `pause_batches` / `resume_batches` stop and restart new Batches only.
22: 
23:   ## Reschedule (ALE-394)
24: 
25:   `reschedule_workshop` moves a scheduled workshop's date, explicit start and end times
26:   and/or venue at any time before Attendance Finalisation; it is refused
27:   only with `:after_finalisation` or `:already_cancelled` (and a pending
28:   Batch never blocks it). Under the Beginners' Workshop lock, then the open
29:   Intakes:
30: 
31:     * the Payment Cutoff keeps its (Dublin civil) offset before the start
32:       unless a new date or time is supplied, and every open Batch window
33:       ending after the new cutoff is brought forward to it;
34:     * while Batch 1 has not gone out, the contact-from date keeps its offset
35:       before the workshop date unless one is supplied (`update_workshop`'s
36:       rules judge a supplied one); a kept date that would fall after the new
37:       cutoff date is brought forward to Dublin today, so Batch 1 goes out at
38:       the next 10:00;
39:     * "Workshop rescheduled" is queued to every open Intake (log occasion
40:       `rescheduled:<n>`); seats, holds and windows' people are untouched;
41:     * the workshop's `reschedule_count` names the reschedule: Pre-workshop
42:       info is owed once per schedule (occasion
43:       `IntakeEmails.Occasion.pre_workshop/1`), so anyone who had it gets it
44:       again at the new cutoff through the same Payment Cutoff pass;
45:     * every Staff member (the actor included) gets a keyed Notification
46:       (`beginners-workshop:<id>:rescheduled:<n>`), signalled after commit.
47: 
48:   Nothing is scheduled per workshop, so no job needs rewriting.
49: 
50:   ## Cancel (ALE-395)
51: 
52:   `cancel_workshop` (`beginners.workshops.manage`, optional `reason` ≤ 500)
53:   cancels a scheduled workshop at any time before Attendance Finalisation
54:   (`:after_finalisation` / `:already_cancelled` otherwise). Under the
55:   Beginners' Workshop lock, then the open Intakes' Waitlist entries, the
56:   open Intakes, those people's live Carried Fees and the workshop's live
57:   Seat Holds and paying payments:
58: 
59:     * every `paid` Intake is deferred exactly as `defer` does it (a
60:       Stripe-paid one creates a `held` Carried Fee, a Carried-Fee-paid
61:       one's fee goes back to `held`), its door check-in is discarded, and
62:       "Workshop cancelled – paid" is queued instead of "Deferred";
63:     * every `contacted` Intake becomes `returned` (the person `waiting`
64:       with their original priority; a holder keeps their `held` fee), its
65:       live Seat Hold `releasing`, and "Workshop cancelled – unpaid" is
66:       queued — both with log occasion `cancelled`;
67:     * each Intake gets a `cancel_workshop` history row carrying the reason;
68:     * every Staff member (the actor included) gets the keyed Notification
69:       `beginners-workshop:<id>:cancelled`, signalled after commit.
70: 
71:   Every time-driven pass, the Intake page's commands and the door judge
72:   `status = scheduled`, so nothing happens to the workshop afterwards. A
73:   completion that arrives for a `releasing` hold is refunded in full by
74:   `complete_payment`'s `paid_after_close`. People move to another workshop
75:   by being fast-tracked there as Carried Fee holders, who then confirm.
76: 
77:   ## Cross-family calls
78: 
79:   Staff is `Commands.Staff`'s: `schedule_workshop` reads and applies
80:   optional Staff through `Staff.staff_input/1` and `Staff.apply_staff/4`,
81:   and the reschedule and cancel Notifications go through
82:   `Staff.notify_each_staff/3`, worded by `NotificationCopy`. A family never
83:   calls another family's private functions (ALE-405).
84:   """

See `docs/workshop-calendar.md` for the shared participant protocol.

See `docs/workshop-calendar.md` for privacy recovery and external-copy limits.

Stubs reach Tasks/inline jobs via `$callers`; other processes need `Req.Test.allow/3`. Shared subscription-payment decoding lives in `Dhc.Stripe.SubscriptionPayment` and the one retry rule in `Dhc.Stripe.Failure.retryable?/1`; see "Stubbing Stripe" in `docs/agents/notes.md`.

- Use the already included and available `:req` (`Req`) library for HTTP requests, **avoid** `:httpoison`, `:tesla`, and `:httpc`. Req is included by default and is the preferred HTTP client for Phoenix apps

### Phoenix v1.8 guidelines

- **Always** begin your LiveView templates with `<Layouts.app flash={@flash} ...>` which wraps all inner content
- The `MyAppWeb.Layouts` module is aliased in the `my_app_web.ex` file, so you can use it without needing to alias it again
- Anytime you run into errors with no `current_scope` assign:
  - You failed to follow the Authenticated Routes guidelines, or you failed to pass `current_scope` to `<Layouts.app>`
  - **Always** fix the `current_scope` error by moving your routes to the proper `live_session` and ensure you pass `current_scope` as needed
- Phoenix v1.8 moved the `<.flash_group>` component to the `Layouts` module. You are **forbidden** from calling `<.flash_group>` outside of the `layouts.ex` module

- **Always** use the imported `<.input>` component for form inputs from `core_components.ex` when available. `<.input>` is imported and using it will save steps and prevent errors

custom classes must fully style the input


<!-- usage-rules-start -->

<!-- phoenix:elixir-start -->
## Elixir guidelines

- Elixir lists **do not support index based access via the access syntax**

  **Never do this (invalid)**:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      mylist[i]

  Instead, **always** use `Enum.at`, pattern matching, or `List` for index based list access, ie:

      i = 0
      mylist = ["blue", "green"]
      Enum.at(mylist, i)

- Elixir variables are immutable, but can be rebound, so for block expressions like `if`, `case`, `cond`, etc
  you *must* bind the result of the expression to a variable if you want to use it and you CANNOT rebind the result inside the expression, ie:

      # INVALID: we are rebinding inside the `if` and the result never gets assigned
      if connected?(socket) do
        socket = assign(socket, :val, val)
      end

      # VALID: we rebind the result of the `if` to a new variable
      socket =
        if connected?(socket) do
          assign(socket, :val, val)
        end

- **Never** nest multiple modules in the same file as it can cause cyclic dependencies and compilation errors
- **Never** use map access syntax (`changeset[:field]`) on structs as they do not implement the Access behaviour by default. For regular structs, you **must** access the fields directly, such as `my_struct.field` or use higher level APIs that are available on the struct if they exist, `Ecto.Changeset.get_field/2` for changesets
- Elixir's standard library has everything necessary for date and time manipulation. Familiarize yourself with the common `Time`, `Date`, `DateTime`, and `Calendar` interfaces by accessing their documentation as necessary. The one sanctioned date/time dependency is `tz`, the IANA database behind `Dhc.ClubCalendar`'s Europe/Dublin conversions. **Never** install additional dependencies unless asked or for date/time parsing (which you can use the `date_time_parser` package)
- Don't use `String.to_atom/1` on user input (memory leak risk)
- Predicate function names should not start with `is_` and should end in a question mark. Names like `is_thing` should be reserved for guards
- Elixir's builtin OTP primitives like `DynamicSupervisor` and `Registry`, require names in the child spec, such as `{DynamicSupervisor, name: MyApp.MyDynamicSup}`, then you can use `DynamicSupervisor.start_child(MyApp.MyDynamicSup, child_spec)`
- Use `Task.async_stream(collection, callback, options)` for concurrent enumeration with back-pressure. The majority of times you will want to pass `timeout: :infinity` as option

## Mix guidelines

- Read the docs and options before using tasks (by using `mix help task_name`)
- To debug test failures, run tests in a specific file with `mix test test/my_test.exs` or run all previously failed tests with `mix test --failed`
- `mix deps.clean --all` is **almost never needed**. **Avoid** using it unless you have good reason

## Test guidelines

- **Always use `start_supervised!/1`** to start processes in tests as it guarantees cleanup between tests
- **Avoid** `Process.sleep/1` and `Process.alive?/1` in tests
  - Instead of sleeping to wait for a process to finish, **always** use `Process.monitor/1` and assert on the DOWN message:

      ref = Process.monitor(pid)
      assert_receive {:DOWN, ^ref, :process, ^pid, :normal}

   - Instead of sleeping to synchronize before the next call, **always** use `_ = :sys.get_state/1` to ensure the process has handled prior messages
<!-- phoenix:elixir-end -->

<!-- phoenix:phoenix-start -->
## Phoenix guidelines

- Remember Phoenix router `scope` blocks include an optional alias which is prefixed for all routes within the scope. **Always** be mindful of this when creating routes within a scope to avoid duplicate module prefixes.

- You **never** need to create your own `alias` for route definitions! The `scope` provides the alias, ie:

      scope "/admin", AppWeb.Admin do
        pipe_through :browser

        live "/users", UserLive, :index
      end

  the UserLive route would point to the `AppWeb.Admin.UserLive` module

- `Phoenix.View` no longer is needed or included with Phoenix, don't use it
<!-- phoenix:phoenix-end -->

<!-- phoenix:ecto-start -->
## Ecto Guidelines

- **Always** preload Ecto associations in queries when they'll be accessed in templates, ie a message that needs to reference the `message.user.email`
- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed
- You **must** use `Ecto.Changeset.get_field(changeset, :field)` to access changeset fields
- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct
- **Always** invoke `mix ecto.gen.migration migration_name_using_underscores` when generating migration files, so the correct timestamp and conventions are applied
<!-- phoenix:ecto-end -->

<!-- usage-rules-end -->

- Remember `import Ecto.Query` and other supporting modules when you write `seeds.exs`
- `Ecto.Schema` fields always use the `:string` type, even for `:text`, columns, ie: `field :name, :string`
- `Ecto.Changeset.validate_number/2` **DOES NOT SUPPORT the `:allow_nil` option**. By default, Ecto validations only run if a change for the given field exists and the change value is not nil, so such as option is never needed

- Fields which are set programmatically, such as `user_id`, must not be listed in `cast` calls or similar for security purposes. Instead they must be explicitly set when creating the struct

10:   table.

1: defmodule Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakePage do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   The person's Intake page read model (ALE-381; ALE-374 "Intake link and
4:   Intake page"): what an Intake link shows. No lock and no actor — the link
5:   is the capability, and an unknown link is `{:error, :not_found}`.
6: 
7:   The view is closed and its `state` is the discriminator:
8: 
9:     * `pay` — a `contacted` Intake before the Payment Cutoff with a free seat,
10:       or with its own live Seat Hold (then the action continues that
11:       checkout instead of starting one);
12:     * `payment_in_progress` — the person came back from a checkout whose
13:       session is still open on our side, or their hold ran out and Stripe has
14:       not ended it yet; the page refreshes until Phoenix reports `paid`;
15:     * `confirm` (ALE-388) — a `contacted` Intake whose person holds a `held`
16:       Carried Fee, with a free seat: the action confirms the place with the
17:       fee instead of paying. The Payment Cutoff does not close it (only
18:       Attendance Finalisation does), and it carries no fee;
19:     * `full` — every seat is paid or held; seats may free up before the
20:       cutoff, so the action checks again (a Carried Fee holder keeps their
21:       fee and may check again until finalisation);
22:     * `paid`;
23:     * `closed` — `inactive` for an Intake that is no longer open (or whose
24:       workshop is no longer scheduled), `payment_closed` for a contacted
25:       Intake after the Payment Cutoff.
26: 
27:   It carries the first name, the
28:   workshop date, start time and venue, the fee and one action — never ids or
29:   Stripe objects; an `inactive` page carries none of them. Seats come from
30:   the same `WorkshopFacts` and `WorkshopPolicy` the boundary decides with, so
31:   a stale page can be out of date but never judge differently.
32:   """
33: 
34:   import Ecto.Query
35: 
36:   alias Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.{
37:     BeginnersWorkshop,
38:     CarriedFee,
39:     Clock,
40:     Intake,
41:     IntakeLink,
42:     IntakePayment,
43:     WorkshopFacts,
44:     WorkshopPolicy
45:   }
46: 
47:   alias Dhc.Repo
48:   alias Dhc.UserProfiles.UserProfile
49: 
50:   @type state :: :pay | :confirm | :payment_in_progress | :full | :paid | :closed
51:   @type action :: :pay | :confirm | :continue_payment | :check_again | :none
52: 
53:   @type t :: %{
54:           state: state(),
55:           action: action(),
56:           closed_reason: :inactive | :payment_closed | nil,
57:           first_name: String.t() | nil,
58:           workshop:
59:             %{date: Date.t(), start_time: Time.t(), end_time: Time.t() | nil, venue: String.t()}
60:             | nil,
61:           fee_cents: pos_integer() | nil,
62:           payment_cutoff: DateTime.t() | nil
63:         }
64: 
65:   @doc "Every state, in display order."
66:   @spec states() :: [state()]
67:   def states, do: [:pay, :confirm, :payment_in_progress, :full, :paid, :closed]
68: 
69:   @doc """
70:   The page behind `token` at the clock's reading. Option `returned_session:`
71:   is the Checkout Session id the person was sent back with (the success
72:   return): while that session's hold is still open, the page is
73:   `payment_in_progress`.
74:   """
75:   @spec show(String.t(), Clock.t(), keyword()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, :not_found}
76:   def show(token, %Clock{} = clock, opts \\ []) when is_binary(token) do
77:     hash = IntakeLink.hash(token)
78: 
79:     from(i in Intake,
80:       join: w in BeginnersWorkshop,
81:       on: w.id == i.workshop_id,
82:       where: i.link_token_hash == ^hash,
83:       select: {i, w}
84:     )
85:     |> Repo.one()
86:     |> case do
87:       nil -> {:error, :not_found}
88:       {intake, workshop} -> {:ok, view(intake, workshop, Clock.read(clock), opts)}
89:     end
90:   end
91: 
92:   defp view(intake, workshop, reading, opts) do
93:     hold = open_hold(intake)
94:     holder? = holder?(intake)
95:     context = %{hold: hold, holder?: holder?, returned: Keyword.get(opts, :returned_session)}
96: 
97:     case decide(intake, workshop, context, reading) do
98:       {:closed, :inactive} ->
99:         %{
100:           state: :closed,
101:           action: :none,
102:           closed_reason: :inactive,
103:           first_name: nil,
104:           workshop: nil,
105:           fee_cents: nil,
106:           payment_cutoff: nil
107:         }
108: 
109:       {state, action, closed_reason} ->
110:         %{
111:           state: state,
112:           action: action,
113:           closed_reason: closed_reason,
114:           first_name: first_name(intake),
115:           workshop: %{
116:             date: workshop.date,
117:             start_time: workshop.start_time,
118:             end_time: workshop.end_time,
119:             venue: workshop.venue
120:           },
121:           fee_cents: fee_cents(intake, workshop, hold, holder?),
122:           payment_cutoff: if(action == :pay, do: workshop.payment_cutoff)
123:         }
124:     end
125:   end
126: 
127:   # A prepaid seat has no fee to show (ALE-388).
128:   defp fee_cents(_intake, _workshop, %IntakePayment{amount_cents: cents}, _holder?), do: cents
129:   defp fee_cents(%Intake{paid_via: "carried_fee"}, _workshop, nil, _holder?), do: nil
130:   defp fee_cents(%Intake{state: "contacted"}, _workshop, nil, true), do: nil
131:   defp fee_cents(_intake, workshop, nil, _holder?), do: workshop.fee_cents
132: 
133:   defp decide(%Intake{state: "paid"}, _workshop, _context, _reading),
134:     do: {:paid, :none, nil}
135: 
136:   defp decide(
137:          %Intake{state: "contacted"},
138:          %BeginnersWorkshop{status: "scheduled"} = w,
139:          %{hold: hold, returned: ret} = context,
140:          r
141:        ) do
142:     cond do
143:       hold && (expired?(hold, r) or returned_to?(hold, ret)) ->
144:         {:payment_in_progress, :check_again, nil}
145: 
146:       hold ->
147:         {:pay, :continue_payment, nil}
148: 
149:       context.holder? ->
150:         holder_page(w)
151: 
152:       not WorkshopPolicy.payment_open?(w, r) ->
153:         {:closed, :none, :payment_closed}
154: 
155:       not WorkshopPolicy.seat_free?(w, facts(w)) ->
156:         {:full, :check_again, nil}
157: 
158:       true ->
159:         {:pay, :pay, nil}
160:     end
161:   end
162: 
163:   defp decide(_intake, _workshop, _context, _reading), do: {:closed, :inactive}
164: 
165:   # A Carried Fee holder: the same seat rule as `confirm`, and never closed
166:   # by the cutoff.
167:   defp holder_page(workshop) do
168:     if WorkshopPolicy.seat_free?(workshop, facts(workshop)),
169:       do: {:confirm, :confirm, nil},
170:       else: {:full, :check_again, nil}
171:   end
172: 
173:   defp expired?(hold, reading), do: DateTime.compare(hold.expires_at, reading.now) != :gt
174: 
175:   defp returned_to?(%IntakePayment{stripe_checkout_session_id: id}, returned)
176:        when is_binary(id) and is_binary(returned),
177:        do: id == returned
178: 
179:   defp returned_to?(_hold, _returned), do: false
180: 
181:   defp holder?(%Intake{waitlist_id: nil}), do: false
182: 
183:   defp holder?(%Intake{waitlist_id: waitlist_id}),
184:     do:
185:       Repo.exists?(
186:         from(f in CarriedFee, where: f.waitlist_id == ^waitlist_id and f.status == "held")
187:       )
188: 
189:   defp open_hold(%Intake{id: id}),
190:     do: Repo.one(from(p in IntakePayment, where: p.intake_id == ^id and p.status == "open"))
191: 
192:   defp facts(%BeginnersWorkshop{id: id}), do: Map.fetch!(WorkshopFacts.load([id]), id)
193: 
194:   defp first_name(%Intake{waitlist_id: nil}), do: nil
195: 
196:   defp first_name(%Intake{waitlist_id: waitlist_id}) do
197:     Repo.one(
198:       from(p in UserProfile, where: p.waitlist_id == ^waitlist_id, limit: 1, select: p.first_name)
199:     )
200:   end
201: end

1: defmodule Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakePage do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   The person's Intake page read model (ALE-381; ALE-374 "Intake link and
4:   Intake page"): what an Intake link shows. No lock and no actor — the link
5:   is the capability, and an unknown link is `{:error, :not_found}`.
6: 
7:   The view is closed and its `state` is the discriminator:
8: 
9:     * `pay` — a `contacted` Intake before the Payment Cutoff with a free seat,
10:       or with its own live Seat Hold (then the action continues that
11:       checkout instead of starting one);
12:     * `payment_in_progress` — the person came back from a checkout whose
13:       session is still open on our side, or their hold ran out and Stripe has
14:       not ended it yet; the page refreshes until Phoenix reports `paid`;
15:     * `confirm` (ALE-388) — a `contacted` Intake whose person holds a `held`
16:       Carried Fee, with a free seat: the action confirms the place with the
17:       fee instead of paying. The Payment Cutoff does not close it (only
18:       Attendance Finalisation does), and it carries no fee;
19:     * `full` — every seat is paid or held; seats may free up before the
20:       cutoff, so the action checks again (a Carried Fee holder keeps their
21:       fee and may check again until finalisation);
22:     * `paid`;
23:     * `closed` — `inactive` for an Intake that is no longer open (or whose
24:       workshop is no longer scheduled), `payment_closed` for a contacted
25:       Intake after the Payment Cutoff.
26: 
27:   It carries the first name, the
28:   workshop date, start time and venue, the fee and one action — never ids or
29:   Stripe objects; an `inactive` page carries none of them. Seats come from
30:   the same `WorkshopFacts` and `WorkshopPolicy` the boundary decides with, so
31:   a stale page can be out of date but never judge differently.
32:   """
33: 
34:   import Ecto.Query
35: 
36:   alias Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.{
37:     BeginnersWorkshop,
38:     CarriedFee,
39:     Clock,
40:     Intake,
41:     IntakeLink,
42:     IntakePayment,
43:     WorkshopFacts,
44:     WorkshopPolicy
45:   }
46: 
47:   alias Dhc.Repo
48:   alias Dhc.UserProfiles.UserProfile
49: 
50:   @type state :: :pay | :confirm | :payment_in_progress | :full | :paid | :closed
51:   @type action :: :pay | :confirm | :continue_payment | :check_again | :none
52: 
53:   @type t :: %{
54:           state: state(),
55:           action: action(),
56:           closed_reason: :inactive | :payment_closed | nil,
57:           first_name: String.t() | nil,
58:           workshop:
59:             %{date: Date.t(), start_time: Time.t(), end_time: Time.t() | nil, venue: String.t()}
60:             | nil,
61:           fee_cents: pos_integer() | nil,
62:           payment_cutoff: DateTime.t() | nil
63:         }
64: 
65:   @doc "Every state, in display order."
66:   @spec states() :: [state()]
67:   def states, do: [:pay, :confirm, :payment_in_progress, :full, :paid, :closed]
68: 
69:   @doc """
70:   The page behind `token` at the clock's reading. Option `returned_session:`
71:   is the Checkout Session id the person was sent back with (the success
72:   return): while that session's hold is still open, the page is
73:   `payment_in_progress`.
74:   """
75:   @spec show(String.t(), Clock.t(), keyword()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, :not_found}
76:   def show(token, %Clock{} = clock, opts \\ []) when is_binary(token) do
77:     hash = IntakeLink.hash(token)
78: 
79:     from(i in Intake,
80:       join: w in BeginnersWorkshop,
81:       on: w.id == i.workshop_id,
82:       where: i.link_token_hash == ^hash,
83:       select: {i, w}
84:     )
85:     |> Repo.one()
86:     |> case do
87:       nil -> {:error, :not_found}
88:       {intake, workshop} -> {:ok, view(intake, workshop, Clock.read(clock), opts)}
89:     end
90:   end
91: 
92:   defp view(intake, workshop, reading, opts) do
93:     hold = open_hold(intake)
94:     holder? = holder?(intake)
95:     context = %{hold: hold, holder?: holder?, returned: Keyword.get(opts, :returned_session)}
96: 
97:     case decide(intake, workshop, context, reading) do
98:       {:closed, :inactive} ->
99:         %{
100:           state: :closed,
101:           action: :none,
102:           closed_reason: :inactive,
103:           first_name: nil,
104:           workshop: nil,
105:           fee_cents: nil,
106:           payment_cutoff: nil
107:         }
108: 
109:       {state, action, closed_reason} ->
110:         %{
111:           state: state,
112:           action: action,
113:           closed_reason: closed_reason,
114:           first_name: first_name(intake),
115:           workshop: %{
116:             date: workshop.date,
117:             start_time: workshop.start_time,
118:             end_time: workshop.end_time,
119:             venue: workshop.venue
120:           },
121:           fee_cents: fee_cents(intake, workshop, hold, holder?),
122:           payment_cutoff: if(action == :pay, do: workshop.payment_cutoff)
123:         }
124:     end
125:   end
126: 
127:   # A prepaid seat has no fee to show (ALE-388).
128:   defp fee_cents(_intake, _workshop, %IntakePayment{amount_cents: cents}, _holder?), do: cents
129:   defp fee_cents(%Intake{paid_via: "carried_fee"}, _workshop, nil, _holder?), do: nil
130:   defp fee_cents(%Intake{state: "contacted"}, _workshop, nil, true), do: nil
131:   defp fee_cents(_intake, workshop, nil, _holder?), do: workshop.fee_cents
132: 
133:   defp decide(%Intake{state: "paid"}, _workshop, _context, _reading),
134:     do: {:paid, :none, nil}
135: 
136:   defp decide(
137:          %Intake{state: "contacted"},
138:          %BeginnersWorkshop{status: "scheduled"} = w,
139:          %{hold: hold, returned: ret} = context,
140:          r
141:        ) do
142:     cond do
143:       hold && (expired?(hold, r) or returned_to?(hold, ret)) ->
144:         {:payment_in_progress, :check_again, nil}
145: 
146:       hold ->
147:         {:pay, :continue_payment, nil}
148: 
149:       context.holder? ->
150:         holder_page(w)
151: 
152:       not WorkshopPolicy.payment_open?(w, r) ->
153:         {:closed, :none, :payment_closed}
154: 
155:       not WorkshopPolicy.seat_free?(w, facts(w)) ->
156:         {:full, :check_again, nil}
157: 
158:       true ->
159:         {:pay, :pay, nil}
160:     end
161:   end
162: 
163:   defp decide(_intake, _workshop, _context, _reading), do: {:closed, :inactive}
164: 
165:   # A Carried Fee holder: the same seat rule as `confirm`, and never closed
166:   # by the cutoff.
167:   defp holder_page(workshop) do
168:     if WorkshopPolicy.seat_free?(workshop, facts(workshop)),
169:       do: {:confirm, :confirm, nil},
170:       else: {:full, :check_again, nil}
171:   end
172: 
173:   defp expired?(hold, reading), do: DateTime.compare(hold.expires_at, reading.now) != :gt
174: 
175:   defp returned_to?(%IntakePayment{stripe_checkout_session_id: id}, returned)
176:        when is_binary(id) and is_binary(returned),
177:        do: id == returned
178: 
179:   defp returned_to?(_hold, _returned), do: false
180: 
181:   defp holder?(%Intake{waitlist_id: nil}), do: false
182: 
183:   defp holder?(%Intake{waitlist_id: waitlist_id}),
184:     do:
185:       Repo.exists?(
186:         from(f in CarriedFee, where: f.waitlist_id == ^waitlist_id and f.status == "held")
187:       )
188: 
189:   defp open_hold(%Intake{id: id}),
190:     do: Repo.one(from(p in IntakePayment, where: p.intake_id == ^id and p.status == "open"))
191: 
192:   defp facts(%BeginnersWorkshop{id: id}), do: Map.fetch!(WorkshopFacts.load([id]), id)
193: 
194:   defp first_name(%Intake{waitlist_id: nil}), do: nil
195: 
196:   defp first_name(%Intake{waitlist_id: waitlist_id}) do
197:     Repo.one(
198:       from(p in UserProfile, where: p.waitlist_id == ^waitlist_id, limit: 1, select: p.first_name)
199:     )
200:   end
201: end

1: defmodule DhcWeb.BeginnersWorkshopIntakeController do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   The `beginnersWorkshopIntake` slice (ALE-381): the person's Intake link.
4:   Public — the token in the path is the capability — and served through the
5:   `:intake_link` pipeline (`Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, redacted request
6:   log). Every response is the closed `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.IntakePage`
7:   view or a refusal. The payment command alone returns the credentials to
8:   mount embedded Checkout (or resume a pre-migration hosted session), never
9:   a payment row or a Stripe object.
10:   """
11:   use DhcWeb, :controller
12: 
13:   action_fallback DhcWeb.BeginnersWorkshopIntakeHTTP
14: 
15:   alias Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops
16: 
17:   @doc "GET /beginners/intake/{token}"
18:   def show(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
19:     with {:ok, page} <- BeginnersWorkshops.intake_page(token) do
20:       render(conn, :show, page: page)
21:     end
22:   end
23: 
24:   @doc "POST /beginners/intake/{token}/payment — takes the Seat Hold; answers Checkout credentials."
25:   def start_payment(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
26:     case link_command(token, :start_payment) do
27:       {:ok, checkout} -> render(conn, :checkout, checkout: checkout)
28:       {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason}
29:     end
30:   end
31: 
32:   @doc """
33:   POST /beginners/intake/{token}/confirm — a Carried Fee holder confirms
34:   their place (ALE-388); answers the page.
35:   """
36:   def confirm(conn, %{"token" => token}) do
37:     with {:ok, _outcome} <- link_command(token, :confirm),
38:          {:ok, page} <- BeginnersWorkshops.intake_page(token),
39:          do: render(conn, :show, page: page)
40:   end
41: 
42:   @doc """
43:   POST /beginners/intake/{token}/return — the Checkout success return:
44:   completes the payment from the session retrieved server-side, then
45:   answers the page. A completion that cannot finish yet (Stripe unreachable,
46:   session still open) leaves the page `payment_in_progress`.
47:   """
48:   def return_from_checkout(conn, %{"token" => token} = params) do
49:     session_id = params |> Map.get("sessionId") |> session_id()
50: 
51:     with {:ok, _page} <- BeginnersWorkshops.intake_page(token) do
52:       if session_id, do: _ = BeginnersWorkshops.execute(:stripe, {:complete_payment, session_id})
53: 
54:       with {:ok, page} <- BeginnersWorkshops.intake_page(token, returned_session: session_id) do
55:         render(conn, :show, page: page)
56:       end
57:     end
58:   end
59: 
60:   # A malformed token is refused before any read; it is still just an
61:   # unknown link.
62:   defp link_command(token, command) do
63:     case BeginnersWorkshops.execute({:intake_link, token}, command) do
64:       {:error, :forbidden} -> {:error, :not_found}
65:       result -> result
66:     end
67:   end
68: 
69:   # A Checkout Session id (`cs_…`); anything else is ignored.
70:   defp session_id("cs_" <> _rest = id) when byte_size(id) <= 255, do: id
71:   defp session_id(_other), do: nil
72: end

2:   @moduledoc """
3:   Domain-neutral rules for a workshop destination (ALE-438/ALE-440).
4: 
5:   A destination is the optional detail a short venue label alone cannot give an
6:   attendee: a recognizable name and address for the same place, plus an
7:   optional manually supplied Google Maps link used for directions. The label
8:   stays required and independent in every source context; a destination never
9:   replaces it.
10: 
11:   This module owns the two rules every workshop-owning context shares:
12: 
13:     * which manually supplied URLs are supported HTTPS Maps destinations, and
14:     * how a destination composes the recognizable Calendar location string,
15:       falling back to the source's own label when no destination is stored.
16: 
17:   It is deliberately free of workshop policy: storage, commands and scheduling
18:   stay with each source context (ADR 0029), and no provider response shape or
19:   provider identity lives here — a Google-selected destination (later work)
20:   will reuse these seams without either context importing the other.
21: 
22:   ## URL scope
23: 
24:   Only `https` links on Google's Maps surfaces are accepted: executable and
25:   non-secure schemes, embedded credentials, explicit ports, and hosts or paths
26:   outside Maps are refused. The check is a safety allowlist, not an attempt to
27:   prove the link resolves to a particular place; a name/address remains useful
28:   without a link, and a link without a provider listing is a valid destination.

33:   @url_max 2048

35:   # `google.com` hosts serve Maps under a `/maps` path prefix; the dedicated
36:   # `maps.google.com` host is Maps-only, so any path is a Maps destination.
37:   @google_maps_path_hosts ~w(www.google.com google.com)
38:   @google_hosts ~w(maps.google.com)
39:   # Short-link hosts exist only for Maps, so any path is a Maps destination.
40:   @short_link_hosts ~w(maps.app.goo.gl)
41: 
42:   # Hosts whose links are Maps only when the path says so.
43:   @short_link_maps_path_hosts ~w(goo.gl g.co)
44: 
45:   @type url_error ::
46:           :invalid_url | :unsupported_scheme | :credentials | :unsupported_target
47: 
48:   @doc """
49:   The maximum length of a destination name.
50:   """
51:   @spec name_max() :: pos_integer()
52:   def name_max, do: @name_max
53: 
54:   @doc """
55:   The maximum length of a destination address.
56:   """
57:   @spec address_max() :: pos_integer()
58:   def address_max, do: @address_max
59: 
60:   @doc """
61:   The maximum length of a manually supplied directions link.
62:   """
63:   @spec url_max() :: pos_integer()
64:   def url_max, do: @url_max
65: 
66:   @doc """
67:   Trims optional destination text, treating an empty string as absent.
68: 
69:   Both source contexts normalize destination input through this so an emptied
70:   form field clears the stored detail instead of persisting whitespace.
71:   """
72:   @spec normalize_optional(String.t() | nil) :: String.t() | nil
73:   def normalize_optional(nil), do: nil
74: 
75:   def normalize_optional(text) when is_binary(text) do
76:     case String.trim(text) do
77:       "" -> nil
78:       trimmed -> trimmed
79:     end
80:   end
81: 
82:   @doc """
83:   Whether a manually supplied directions link is a supported HTTPS Maps
84:   destination.
85: 
86:   `nil` (no link) is always allowed: the link is optional. Every refusal is a
87:   named reason from the closed `t:url_error/0` set.
88:   """
89:   @spec validate_maps_url(String.t() | nil) :: :ok | {:error, url_error()}
90:   def validate_maps_url(nil), do: :ok
91: 
92:   def validate_maps_url(url) when is_binary(url) do
93:     with :ok <- check_length(url),
94:          {:ok, uri} <- parse(url),
95:          :ok <- check_scheme(uri),
96:          :ok <- check_credentials(uri) do
97:       check_target(uri)
98:     end
99:   end
100: 
101:   def validate_maps_url(_other), do: {:error, :invalid_url}
102: 
103:   @doc """
104:   The one user-facing sentence for each `validate_maps_url/1` refusal.
105: 
106:   Source contexts render this as the field message on their own directions-link
107:   field, so both contexts word the same refusal the same way.
108:   """
109:   @spec url_error_message(url_error()) :: String.t()
110:   def url_error_message(:invalid_url), do: "Directions link must be a valid URL"
111:   def url_error_message(:unsupported_scheme), do: "Directions link must be an https link"
112: 
113:   def url_error_message(:credentials),
114:     do: "Directions link must not include a username or password"
115: 
116:   def url_error_message(:unsupported_target),
117:     do: "Directions link must be a Google Maps link"
118: 
119:   @doc """
120:   Composes the Calendar location string from a destination's name and address,
121:   falling back to the source's own venue label when neither is stored.
122: 
123:   The result is recognizable free-form text for Google's native event location
124:   field — never a link, and never a fabricated place for an unreviewed label.
125:   A destination with only a link keeps the label, because a URL is not a
126:   location people can read.
127:   """
128:   @spec calendar_location(String.t() | nil, String.t() | nil, String.t() | nil) ::
129:           String.t()
130:   def calendar_location(name, address, label) do
131:     composed =
132:       [name, address]
133:       |> Enum.map(&normalize_optional/1)
134:       |> Enum.reject(&is_nil/1)
135:       |> Enum.join(", ")
136: 
137:     if composed == "", do: normalize_optional(label) || "", else: composed
138:   end
139: 
140:   # ── URL checks ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
141: 
142:   defp check_length(url) do
143:     if String.length(url) <= @url_max,
144:       do: :ok,
145:       else: {:error, :invalid_url}
146:   end
147: 
148:   defp parse(url) do
149:     case URI.new(url) do
150:       {:ok, %URI{} = uri} -> {:ok, uri}
151:       {:error, _part} -> {:error, :invalid_url}
152:     end
153:   end
154: 
155:   defp check_scheme(%URI{scheme: scheme}) do
156:     if scheme != nil and String.downcase(scheme) == "https",
157:       do: :ok,
158:       else: {:error, :unsupported_scheme}
159:   end
160: 
161:   defp check_credentials(%URI{userinfo: nil}), do: :ok
162:   defp check_credentials(%URI{}), do: {:error, :credentials}
163: 
164:   # `URI.new/1` fills in the scheme's default port (443 for https), so only a
165:   # non-default explicit port is refused; no Maps share link carries one.
166:   defp check_target(%URI{port: port}) when is_integer(port) and port != 443,
167:     do: {:error, :unsupported_target}
168: 
169:   defp check_target(%URI{host: host, path: path}) when is_binary(host) do
170:     host = host |> String.downcase() |> String.trim_trailing(".")
171: 
172:     cond do
173:       host in @google_maps_path_hosts -> maps_path?(path)
174:       host in @google_hosts -> :ok
175:       host in @short_link_hosts -> :ok
176:       host in @short_link_maps_path_hosts -> maps_path?(path)
177:       true -> {:error, :unsupported_target}
178:     end
179:   end
180: 
181:   defp check_target(_uri), do: {:error, :invalid_url}
182: 
183:   defp maps_path?(path) do
184:     if path in ["/maps", "/maps/"] or String.starts_with?(path || "", "/maps/"),
185:       do: :ok,
186:       else: {:error, :unsupported_target}
187:   end
188: end

1: defmodule Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.Commands do
2:   @moduledoc """
3:   ALE-378 (ADR 0029 and its amendments): the one interface of every
4:   Beginners' Workshop write. `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.execute/3` delegates
5:   here; nothing else in the context opens a write transaction (the one
6:   `Repo.transaction` is `Commands.Protocol.transact/1`). Staff commands,
7:   the person's Intake-page commands, Stripe-driven commands and time-driven
8:   passes all arrive as a `command` with an `actor`. This module authorizes
9:   the actor and routes the command to its family module; it holds no
10:   command logic.
11: 
12:   ## The protocol
13: 
14:   Every command body runs inside the protocol core,
15:   `Dhc.BeginnersWorkshops.Commands.Protocol` (ADR 0029, second amendment):
16:   `transact/1` around `with_locked/2`, the clock read under the lock, and
17:   every write through `persist/1` (`transition/3` for a status change).
18:   Its moduledoc holds the transition table, the constraint translation and
19:   the signal-after-commit rule. **The lock order is Beginners' Workshop →
20:   Waitlist entry → Intake → Carried Fee → payment → refund**: a command may
21:   skip levels but never lock upward, and Stripe is called only between
22:   transactions.
23: 
24:   What a closing does to the person — standing, Seat Hold, Carried Fee,
25:   refund, notice — is one row of `Commands.Settlement` (ALE-404), keyed by
26:   cause and ending and run inside the command's `with_locked/2`. A command
27:   decides whether it may run (`IntakePolicy`, `CarriedFeePolicy`,
28:   `WorkshopPolicy`), names the row, and writes its own history row.
29: 
30:   ## Actors
31: 
32:     * `{:staff, principal_id}` — authorized through `Dhc.Auth.Capabilities`
33:       for the command's capability (`@staff_capabilities`) **before any
34:       read**; an assignment-scoped capability (`beginners.workshops.run`) is
35:       decided against the workshop's Staff rows, and a denial conceals the
36:       workshop (`:not_found`);
37:     * `{:intake_link, token}` — the person's Intake page;
38:     * `:stripe` — webhook and success-return completions;
39:     * `:system` — time-driven passes and workers;
40:     * `{:intake_reply, intake_reply_id}` (ALE-411) — a Reply Action: the
41:       command an Intake Reply asked for, run by

content.text: **Planning migration creation with mix help**

mix ecto.gen.migration

Generates a migration.

The repository must be set under `:ecto_repos` in the current app configuration
or given via the `-r` option.

## Examples

    $ mix ecto.gen.migration add_posts_table
    $ mix ecto.gen.migration add_posts_table -r Custom.Repo

The generated migration filename will be prefixed with the current timestamp in
UTC which is used for versioning and ordering.

By default, the migration will be generated to the "priv/YOUR_REPO/migrations"
directory of the current application but it can be configured to be any
subdirectory of `priv` by specifying the `:priv` key under the repository
configuration.

This generator will automatically open the generated file if you have
`ECTO_EDITOR` set in your environment variable.

## Command line options

  * `-r`, `--repo` - the repo to generate migration for
  * `--no-compile` - does not compile applications before running
  * `--no-deps-check` - does not check dependencies before running
  * `--migrations-path` - the path to run the migrations from, defaults to
    `priv/repo/migrations`

## Configuration

If the current app configuration specifies a custom migration module the
generated migration code will use that rather than the default
`Ecto.Migration`:

    config :ecto_sql, migration_module: MyApplication.CustomMigrationModule
